title.narrative: WGG- Building Inclusive Movements and Alliances in Bangladesh

description.narrative: It is a strategic platform for activists to participate in and learn about differing viewpoints, form creative alliances and highlight issues that are generally considered to be beyond the purview of women’s rights and gender justice.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

3 DPOs (Bangladesh Protibondhi Unnion Soyongtha- BPUS, National Grassroots Disability Organization(NGDO) and Agrojatra) represented by 27 Women and Girls with Disabilities learned how to communicate with Government officials and how to participate in Government level programs at the two-day training in Borishal called “Convening dialogue and advocacy” which was held on 22 and 23 Oct 2022. In 2022, strategic partners also focused on internal strengthening in conducting international human rights advocacy (platforms such as CEDAW). This will be escalated to collectives and Young Leaders from 2023.

Participation through various marked days of the calendar including occasions regarding disability day

On four separate ocassions, different group of women with disabilities in Barishal, Dinajpur , Satkhira and khulna (in total 60 women with disabilities) who are working for disability inclusion conducted advocacy meetings with local government. On three different occasions, seven YLs participated in national and international advocacy platform: Six Young Leaders (YLs) from three organizations within the indigenous community of Chittagong Hill Tracts led a virtual session titled 'In between documented and undocumented: Reimagining documentation' on October 30, 2023 during the Global South Women’s Forum on Sustainable Development. The session highlighted the historical challenge of addressing human rights violations due to the lack of documentation in indigenous communities. It emphasized the need to recognize diverse documentation systems, including female-centric oral traditions, to sustain global diversity and equity. On the occasion of ‘International Day of Persons with Disabilities’ a panel discussion was organized by UNRC, UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA, ILO, and Sightsavers in Dhaka. The theme for the panel discussions was 'United in Action to Rescue and Achieve the SDGs For, With and By Persons with Disabilities.' A visually impaired Young Leader from WGG was among the speakers, addressing barriers to employability faced by persons with disabilities. two Young Leaders from Affasa hosted a day-long workshop with youth to empower them with knowledge and skills, followed by a panel discussion featuring District Magistrate, community leaders, and Upazila Vice Chairman, fostering a collective approach to addressing and preventing GBV
Participation through various marked days of the calendar including occasions regarding disability day

The Executive Director of partner org was a speaker for the disability rights movement at International Disability Day, where she advocated for the implementation of the action plan from the Rights and Protection act of PWDs 2013. She also spoke about the budget allocation for disability inclusion in government programs.A rally and discussion meeting on disability inclusion with community members, teachers, and community leaders was held as part of the Campaign on 16 days of Activism.On Autism Day, discussions on collaboration and advocacy with the government focussed on issues on disability inclusion and autism with the presence of organization's staff, beneficiaries, community leaders, and family members.

5 national alliances (Human rights forum BD, CEDAW platform, Disability alliance, citizen alliance on sdgs), 4 international alliances (AWID, APWLD, South Asian Disability Forum, APRCEM) continued, and additional two alliances

One partner joined this new alliance for disability inclusion, creating awareness among them about the rights of W&GWDs. On one occasion a session on CEDAW shadow reporting hosted by a partner for its YLs from diverse backgrounds and movement spaces in building their capacity strengthening and engage in alliance and movement.One partner has been participating in ‘Feminist Faultlines’ an alliance, who came together as like-minded feminists to reflect on, discuss, and engage in collaborative advocacy around ‘faultlines’ (contested themes) within feminist movements, such as positions on sex workers’ rights, identifying and distinguishing ages for sexual consent/minimum age of marriage, and responding to trafficking and gender-based violence (among others).
